We have template 1914386. Need to propose retrosynthesis route for target SMILES: COC(C1(C=C1[Si](C)(C)C)/C=C/C2=CC=CC=C2)=O.

We need to apply this template in retrosynthetic direction (i.e., break target into precursors). The template appears to be a retro SMILES: The retro_smarts_template is given: '[C;D1;H3:9]-[#14:10](-[C;D1;H3:11])(-[C;D1;H3:12])-[C;H0;D3;+0:13]1=[CH;D2;+0:14]-[C;H0;D4;+0:1]-1(/[CH;D2;+0:2]=[CH;D2;+0:3]/[c:4])-[C:5](=[O;D1;H0:6])-[#8:7]-[C;D1;H3:8]>>O=[C;H0;D3;+0:1](-[CH2;D2;+0:2]-[CH2;D2;+0:3]-[c:4])-[C:5](=[O;D1;H0:6])-[#8:7]-[C;D1;H3:8].[C;D1;H3:9]-[#14:10](-[C;D1;H3:11])(-[C;D1;H3:12])-[C;H0;D2;+0:13]#[CH;D1;+0:14]'

So forward reaction (template) is: product (left side) is a molecule with a silyl group attached to a cyclohexadienyl? Actually left side is a complex molecule with Si attached to a carbon that is part of a ring with double bonds etc. The right side (products) are two fragments: an ester (O=C... ) and a silyl alkyne? Wait: The right side shows O=[C;H0;D3;+0:1](-[CH2;D2;+0:2]-[CH2;D2;+0:3]-[c:4])-[C:5](=[O;D1;H0:6])-[#8:7]-[C;D1;H3:8] . That's an ester of phenylpropyl? Actually O=C-CH2-CH2-aryl etc.

And second product: [C;D1;H3:9]-[#14:10](-[C;D1;H3:11])(-[C;D1;H3:12])-[C;H0;D2;+0:13]#[CH;D1;+0:14] which is a silyl-substituted alkyne (maybe TMS-alkyne). So the template is a retro reaction that splits a molecule into an ester fragment and a silyl alkyne fragment.

Our target SMILES: COC(C1(C=C1[Si](C)(C)C)/C=C/C2=CC=CC=C2)=O

Let's parse: It's methyl ester (COC(=O) ...). Actually "COC(...)=O" is methyl ester of something: C O C( ... ) = O. So OCH3 attached to carbonyl carbon. The carbonyl carbon attached to C1(C=C1[Si](C)(C)C)/C=C/C2=CC=CC=C2. So the carbonyl carbon attached to a carbon that is part of a cyclohexadienyl? Let's examine: C1(C=C1[Si](C)(C)C) is a cycloprop? Wait C1(C=C1...) is a cyclobut? Actually "C1(C=C1...)" is a cyclobut? Let's think: "C1(C=C1...)" means a 3-membered ring? The pattern: C1 ... =C1 indicates a 3-membered ring (cyclopropene). But there is also a double bond inside. So it's a cyclopropene with a silyl substituent. Then "/C=C/" attaches to phenyl ring.

Thus the target seems to be an ester of a propenyl phenyl with a silyl cyclopropene.

The template expects a product that contains a silyl alkyne fragment, not a silyl cyclopropene. So maybe not matching.

We need to check if the template matches the target. Use check_smiles_reaction_template_matching.
